issues.description: Global variable 'display_start' is declared in the template and described in the problem statement as the framebuffer base address, but the solution implementation removed the global definition while still referencing the symbol. Problem statement/template: the frame buffer base is named 'display_start' (expected global). Template defines it in .bss (display_start RESB 8294400). Solution: the .asm file contains a comment saying 'display_start moved to local stack scope in main' and does not define the symbol, yet the solution still references 'display_start' (assembly uses at least two sites: set_pixel and main). This will cause an undefined-symbol assembly/link error and confuses students about whether 'display_start' should be a global variable or passed/computed locally.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the treatment of 'display_start' consistent. Option A (simpler / matches template): reintroduce the global definition in the solution .bss section exactly as in the template (display_start RESB 8294400) and remove the misleading comment. Option B (intentional refactor): explicitly pass the base address to set_pixel or compute it and store it in a local named symbol, and update all references to use that local/passed address; also update the problem statement and template comments to document the new calling convention. Ensure comments and code agree so students are not left with undefined-symbol errors.
